name: Édouard Vuillard
findings: Within his own canvases, spanish bistre turns up as a small accent in 71% of the paintings that hold it, 2.0x the archive's rate (from 791 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, parula blue turns up as the lightest note in 100% of the paintings that hold it, 1.8x the archive's rate (from 791 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, madder blue turns up as the shadow in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 3.8x the archive's rate (from 791 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 791 paintings here).
Pairs ash with gnaphalium green more than chance would predict (3 of 791 paintings here).
Pairs grey with plumbago grey more than chance would predict (3 of 791 paintings here).
His single largest palette family (dark walnut, smoky black, linen grey) covers 66% of his paintings here.
Keeps 2 distinct palette families here, from dark walnut, smoky black to dresden brown, sandstone.
